# Percentage composition from molecular formula

## 1. Topic Introduction
A fertilizer bag shouts "46-0-0", a medicine strip lists milligrams per tablet, a steel specification demands 0.2% carbon — all are **percentage composition**: the mass share of each element in a compound. It is the most commercial calculation in chemistry, deciding what farmers pay for, what patients swallow, and what factories must guarantee.

The formula is one line — (element mass ÷ molar mass) × 100 — but it runs both directions: forward from formula to percentages (is this urea really 46% N?), and backward from percentage analysis to empirical and molecular formulae (what is this unknown?). This topic closes the foundation unit by turning every earlier concept into numbers.

**Why it matters.** Percentage composition is the quality-control language of the chemical industry. It connects the molecular formula (which atoms, how many) to the commercial specification (what the buyer pays for). Every subsequent unit — Stoichiometry (yield, purity), Organic (combustion analysis), Applied (fertilizer grades, cement purity) — uses this forward/backward logic.

**What you will learn:** (i) percentage composition from formula; (ii) the urea 46% derivation; (iii) composition → empirical formula; (iv) composition + molar mass → molecular formula; (v) applications in fertilizers, drugs and industry.

**Learning outcomes.** You can: compute any % composition; prove urea's 46% N; derive empirical and molecular formulae from analysis data; and audit a label claim.

## 2. Fundamental Conceptual Understanding

### What percentage composition is
The mass percentage of each element in a compound: %E = (total mass of element E in one mole ÷ molar mass of compound) × 100. The percentages of all elements always sum to 100 — the built-in answer check.

### Why it exists
Chemical formulas tell *which* atoms and *how many*, but commerce and regulation speak in *mass percentages*. A farmer buys nitrogen by the kilogram, not by the mole. A drug label lists milligrams per tablet. A steel spec demands 0.2% carbon. Percentage composition translates molecular identity into commercial language.

### How it works
Forward (formula → %): From molecular formula, get M_r. For each element, (atoms × A_r) ÷ M_r × 100 = %. Sum must be 100. Backward (% → formula): % → grams per 100 g → moles (÷ A_r) → simplest ratio → empirical formula. With M_r (from vapour density, mass spec, colligative properties): n = M_r/E_r → molecular formula.

### Where it occurs
Fertilizer bags (46-0-0), drug labels (mg per tablet), steel certificates (0.2% C), cement quality (CaO%), water analysis (ppm), air quality (%), food labels (%), environmental regulations (ppm/ppb).

### What its components are
Molecular formula, molar mass, element masses per mole, percentage values, empirical formula, molecular formula.

### How components interact
Formula → M_r → element masses → % → sum to 100 (check). % → empirical → M_r → n = M_r/E_r → molecular. Combustion analysis gives %C (×12/44) and %H (×2/18); %O by difference. The loop closes: formula ↔ % ↔ formula.

### What makes it biologically important
Drug potency: % active ingredient in tablet. Nutrient density: % protein (N × 6.25), % fat, % carbohydrate. Blood: % haemoglobin saturation, % CO₂. Quality control: assay % of API in drug. The body reads chemistry in percentages — enzymes saturate at % substrate, receptors occupy at % ligand.

## 3. Scientific Definitions

| Term | Scientific meaning | Explanation | Importance |
|------|-------------------|-------------|-------------|
| Percentage composition | Mass % of each element in a compound | %E = (mass of E per mole ÷ M_r) × 100; Σ%E = 100 | Translates formula to commercial spec |
| Forward calculation | Formula → percentage | Known formula, compute % | Quality audit of label claims |
| Backward calculation | Percentage → formula | Known % (analysis), find formula | Structure elucidation of unknowns |
| Combustion analysis | Burn sample → weigh CO₂, H₂O → %C, %H | %C = mass CO₂ × 12/44; %H = mass H₂O × 2/18; %O by difference | Experimental source of % data |
| Vapour density (VD) | Mass of gas volume ÷ mass of same volume H₂ (same T,P) | M_r = 2 × VD (H₂ = 2 scale) | Classic M_r determination for volatiles |
| Empirical formula | Simplest whole-number atom ratio | From % data: % → g → mol → ratio | First step in formula identification |
| Molecular formula | Actual atom numbers in molecule | Empirical × n; n = M_r/E_r | Unique molecular identity |
| % yield | (Experimental ÷ Theoretical) × 100 | Compares actual to stoichiometric max | Process efficiency |
| Assay | Quantitative determination of main component | Titration, HPLC, spectroscopy | Drug/fertilizer/cement quality control |
| Purity | % of desired substance in sample | Assay % = purity if single component | Commercial grade definition |

**Keywords:** percentage composition, forward/backward, combustion analysis, vapour density, empirical formula, molecular formula, urea 46%, H₂SO₄ shares, CaCO₃ audit, O by difference, 12/44, 2/18, M_r = 2×VD, n = M_r/E_r.

## 4. Detailed Explanation

### 4.1 Percentage composition (forward direction)

| Compound | M_r | % calculation | Result |
|----------|-----|---------------|--------|
| H₂SO₄ | 98 | %H = 2/98×100 = 2.04%; %S = 32/98×100 = 32.65%; %O = 64/98×100 = 65.31% | Sum = 100.00 ✓ |
| Urea CO(NH₂)₂ | 60 | %N = 28/60×100 = 46.67%; %C = 12/60×100 = 20.00%; %O = 16/60×100 = 26.67%; %H = 4/60×100 = 6.67% | Sum = 100.01 ✓ (rounding) |
| NH₄NO₃ | 80 | %N = 28/80×100 = 35.00%; %H = 4/80×100 = 5.00%; %O = 48/80×100 = 60.00% | Sum = 100.00 ✓ |
| CaCO₃ | 100 | %Ca = 40/100×100 = 40%; %C = 12/100×100 = 12%; %O = 48/100×100 = 48% | Sum = 100% |
| Glucose C₆H₁₂O₆ | 180 | %C = 72/180×100 = 40%; %H = 12/180×100 = 6.67%; %O = 96/180×100 = 53.33% | Sum = 100.00 ✓ |

**Assumptions box:** Formula assumed correct and pure; percentages are mass/mass (w/w); analytical data assumed dry and impurity-free unless stated; percentages sum to 100 within rounding.

### 4.2 From analysis back to formula (reverse direction)

**Step-by-step algorithm:**
1. **% → grams:** Assume 100 g sample → % = grams of each element.
2. **Grams → moles:** Divide each by its A_r (C/12, H/1, O/16, N/14, S/32, etc.).
3. **Moles → simplest ratio:** Divide all by smallest mole value. If decimals remain, multiply by 2, 3, etc. to clear to whole numbers.
4. **Write empirical formula** from the ratio.
5. **Find E_r** (sum of A_r in empirical formula).
6. **Obtain M_r** (given, or from vapour density M_r = 2×VD, or mass spec, or colligative properties).
7. **n = M_r / E_r** (must be integer).
8. **Molecular formula = n × empirical formula**.

**Worked example — unknown organic:**
- Data: 40% C, 6.7% H, 53.3% O
- Per 100 g: 40 g C, 6.7 g H, 53.3 g O
- Moles: C = 40/12 = 3.33; H = 6.7/1 = 6.7; O = 53.3/16 = 3.33
- Ratio ÷3.33: C 1, H 2, O 1 → **CH₂O** (E_r = 30)
- If M_r = 180: n = 180/30 = 6 → **C₆H₁₂O₆** (glucose)
- If M_r = 90: n = 90/30 = 3 → **C₃H₆O₃** (lactic acid)
- If M_r = 30: n = 1 → **CH₂O** (formaldehyde)

**Worked example — combustion analysis:**
- 4.4 g sample → 8.8 g CO₂ + 3.6 g H₂O
- %C = 8.8 × 12/44 × 100 / 4.4 = 2.4 × 100 / 4.4 = **54.55%**
- %H = 3.6 × 2/18 × 100 / 4.4 = 0.4 × 100 / 4.4 = **9.09%**
- %O = 100 − 54.55 − 9.09 = **36.36%**
- Moles: C 54.55/12 = 4.55; H 9.09/1 = 9.09; O 36.36/16 = 2.27
- Ratio ÷2.27: C 2, H 4, O 1 → **C₂H₄O** (E_r = 44)
- If M_r = 88: n = 2 → **C₄H₈O₂** (ethyl acetate, etc.)

### 4.3 Fertilizer grade — the commercial % composition
| Fertilizer | Formula | M_r | %N | %P₂O₅ | %K₂O | Label |
|------------|---------|-----|-----|--------|------|------|
| Urea | CO(NH₂)₂ | 60 | 46.67% | — | — | 46-0-0 |
| Ammonium nitrate | NH₄NO₃ | 80 | 35.00% | — | — | 35-0-0 |
| DAP | (NH₄)₂HPO₄ | 132 | 21.2% | 46% | — | 18-46-0 |
| MOP | KCl | 74.5 | — | — | 60% K₂O | 0-0-60 |
| SSP | Ca(H₂PO₄)₂·H₂O + CaSO₄ | — | — | 16% P₂O₅ | — | 0-16-0 |

**Nepal context:** NARC recommends 100 kg urea + 50 kg DAP + 25 kg MOP per hectare for wheat = 46 + 9 + 0 = 55 kg N, 23 kg P₂O₅, 15 kg K₂O per ha.

### 4.4 Comparison: forward vs backward
| Direction | Input | Output | Use case |
|-----------|-------|--------|----------|
| Forward | Molecular formula | % composition | Quality audit, label verification, commercial spec |
| Backward | % composition (analysis) | Empirical formula | Unknown identification, structure elucidation |
| Backward + M_r | % + M_r | Molecular formula | New compound characterization, drug development |
| Combustion | CO₂, H₂O masses | %C, %H, (%O by diff) | Organic analysis lab standard |
| Vapour density | VD | M_r = 2×VD | Volatile unknowns |

### 4.5 Common traps and how to avoid them
| Trap | Wrong | Correct |
|------|-------|---------|
| Sum ≠ 100 | Forgetting an element | Always check sum; missing = that element |
| Mole % vs mass % | Using mole ratios directly | Convert to mass via A_r first |
| O by difference | Assuming only C,H,O present | State assumption; N/S need separate estimation |
| Clearing decimals | Rounding instead of multiplying | Multiply by 2, 3, 4... to get integers |
| n not integer | Rounding M_r or E_r | Re-check data; M_r must be multiple of E_r |
| Same empirical | Assuming same compound | CH₂O family: glucose, formaldehyde, lactic acid — verify M_r |
| VD scale | Using air = 1 instead of H₂ = 2 | VD always H₂ = 2 for M_r = 2×VD |
| Hydrates | Forgetting water of crystallization | Include H₂O in formula mass for % |

### 4.6 Worked numericals (Given → Formula → Substitution → Answer with unit)
1. **H₂SO₄ shares.** M_r 98: %H = 2/98×100 = **2.04%**; %S = 32/98×100 = **32.65%**; %O = 64/98×100 = **65.31%**; sum 100.00 ✓.
2. **Urea proof.** M_r 60: %N = 28/60×100 = **46.67%** ≈ 46 — the bag verified; %C 20%, %O 26.67%, %H 6.67%.
3. **Ammonium nitrate check.** NH₄NO₃, M_r 80: %N = 28/80×100 = **35%** — poorer than urea per kilogram, the comparison farmers pay for.
4. **Empirical from analysis.** 40% C, 6.7% H, 53.3% O → 40/12 = 3.33; 6.7/1 = 6.7; 53.3/16 = 3.33 → ÷3.33 → 1:2:1 → **CH₂O**.
5. **Molecular with M_r.** Above + M_r 180 → E_r 30 → n = 6 → **C₆H₁₂O₆**. With M_r 90 → n = 3 → **C₃H₆O₃** (lactic acid shares the ratio — empirical ≠ identity).
6. **Combustion analysis.** 4.4 g organic → 8.8 g CO₂ + 3.6 g H₂O: C = 8.8×12/44 = 2.4 g (**54.5%**); H = 3.6×2/18 = 0.4 g (**9.1%**); O by difference 36.4% → C:H:O = 4.54:9.1:2.27 → ÷2.27 → 2:4:1 → **C₂H₄O**.
7. **Fertilizer comparison.** Urea N% = 46.67%; NH₄NO₃ N% = 35% — urea delivers more N per rupee at equal price per kg.
8. **Limestone audit.** CaCO₃: %Ca = 40/100 = 40%. A claim of "45% Ca" means impurity or different mineral.

## 6. Chemical Processes and Mechanisms

### Process: Combustion analysis (organic elemental analysis)
1. **Definition:** Burning a known mass of organic compound in excess oxygen; absorbing and weighing the CO₂ and H₂O produced to determine %C and %H.
2. **Location:** Organic analysis laboratory; also automated CHNS/O analysers.
3. **Requirements:** Combustion furnace (CuO, 800°C), O₂ carrier gas, H₂O absorber (Mg(ClO₄)₂ or anhydrous CaCl₂), CO₂ absorber (KOH/Ascarite), analytical balance (±0.1 mg).
4. **Components:** Sample boat, combustion tube, absorption train, balance, data logger.
5. **Sequential steps:** (i) Weigh empty absorbers; (ii) Weigh ~0.1 g sample accurately; (iii) Introduce sample to furnace in O₂ stream; (iv) Combustion: C_xH_yO_z + (x + y/4 − z/2)O₂ → xCO₂ + (y/2)H₂O; (v) Gases pass through H₂O absorber (mass gain = H₂O mass); (vi) Then through CO₂ absorber (mass gain = CO₂ mass); (vii) Re-weigh absorbers; (viii) Calculate: %C = Δm_CO₂ × (12/44) × 100 / m_sample; %H = Δm_H₂O × (2/18) × 100 / m_sample; %O = 100 − %C − %H − %N − %S − ...
6. **Result:** %C, %H, (%O by difference) — the data for empirical formula determination.
7. **Significance:** The classic experimental source of composition data for unknown organic compounds; automated analysers do this in minutes for QC.

### Process: Quality audit by percentage composition
1. **Definition:** Verifying a product's label claim by determining its actual % composition and comparing to specification.
2. **Location:** Fertilizer plant QC lab, cement plant lab, pharmaceutical QC, food testing lab.
3. **Requirements:** Reference methods (titration, gravimetry, spectroscopy), certified reference materials, calibrated instruments.
4. **Components:** Sample divider, grinder, balance, titration setup / HPLC / ICP-OES / XRF, SOPs.
5. **Sequential steps:** (i) Obtain representative sample (coning/quartering); (ii) Prepare test portion (grind, dry, weigh); (iii) Run assay per official method (e.g., urea %N by Kjeldahl/distillation); (iv) Calculate % = (measured / theoretical) × 100; (v) Compare to spec (e.g., urea ≥ 46% N); (vi) Report pass/fail; (vii) If fail, trigger investigation (raw material, process, sampling).
6. **Result:** Certificate of analysis (CoA) with % composition, pass/fail vs spec.
7. **Significance:** Legal requirement for trade; protects farmer (fertilizer), patient (drug), builder (cement), consumer (food).

### Process: Empirical → molecular formula determination (structure elucidation)
1. **Definition:** Identifying a compound's molecular formula from composition data and molar mass.
2. **Location:** Natural products lab, pharmaceutical R&D, forensic lab, environmental analysis.
3. **Requirements:** % composition (CHNS/O analyser), M_r (high-resolution mass spectrometry, or vapour density for volatiles), NMR/IR for structure confirmation.
4. **Components:** Elemental analyser, HRMS (ESI, EI, MALDI), NMR, IR, software (formula calculator).
5. **Sequential steps:** (i) Obtain %C, %H, %N, %S, %O (by difference); (ii) Compute empirical formula (CH₂O, C₂H₄O, etc.); (iv) Obtain exact M_r from HRMS (e.g., 180.0634 for C₆H₁₂O₆); (v) n = M_r/E_r; (vi) Molecular formula = n × empirical; (vii) Confirm with isotope pattern (M+1, M+2) and NMR.
6. **Result:** Unique molecular formula identifying the compound; first step in structure elucidation.
7. **Significance:** Turns anonymous % data into specific molecular identity — essential for new drug/natural product characterization, metabolite ID, pollutant tracking.

## 8. Conceptual Relationships

### Within this topic
- Formula → M_r → element masses → % (forward); % → g → mol → ratio → empirical (backward); empirical + M_r → n = M_r/E_r → molecular (full circle).
- Combustion analysis (12/44, 2/18, O by diff) supplies % data for backward route.
- Vapour density (M_r = 2×VD) supplies M_r for backward route.
- Quality audit uses forward route to verify label claims.

### To other units
- **Stoichiometry:** % yield = (actual/theoretical)×100 uses same % logic; limiting reactant, theoretical yield all connect mass to formula.
- **Organic Chemistry:** Combustion analysis is the standard source of %C/%H for unknowns; empirical/molecular formula is step 1 in structure elucidation.
- **Applied Chemistry:** Fertilizer grade (46-0-0), cement purity (CaO%), drug assay (%API) — all are % composition in commercial language.
- **Modern Manufactures:** Haber process yield, Contact process conversion, Solvay process efficiency — all tracked by % composition of product vs feed.

### To real life
- Farmer reads "46-0-0" and knows 46 kg N per 100 kg bag.
- Cement buyer checks CaO% on CoA — below spec = weak concrete.
- Drug label: 500 mg paracetamol/tablet = assay % of API.
- Steel spec: 0.2% C = 2 kg C per tonne steel.
- Air quality: PM2.5 μg/m³ = % by mass in air volume.
- Food label: % daily value = nutrient mass / recommended intake × 100.

## 9. Important Facts and Scientific Terminology

| Term | Scientific meaning | Explanation | Importance |
|------|-------------------|-------------|-------------|
| % composition formula | %E = (mass of E per mole ÷ M_r) × 100 | Sum of all %E = 100 (built-in check) | Universal forward calculation |
| Combustion factors | C from CO₂: ×12/44; H from H₂O: ×2/18 | Converts oxide mass to element mass | Standard for CHN analysis |
| O by difference | %O = 100 − Σ(%other elements) | Assumes only C,H,O,N,S,halogens present | Necessary when O not measured directly |
| Vapour density (VD) | Mass of gas volume ÷ mass of same volume H₂ | M_r = 2 × VD (H₂ = 2 scale) | Classic M_r for volatiles |
| Empirical formula | Simplest whole-number ratio | From % data: % → g → mol → ratio | First step in formula ID |
| Molecular formula | Actual atom numbers | Empirical × n; n = M_r/E_r | Unique molecular identity |
| n = M_r/E_r | Multiplier from empirical to molecular | Must be integer; if not, re-check data | Bridges empirical to molecular |
| CH₂O family | Glucose C₆H₁₂O₆, formaldehyde CH₂O, lactic acid C₃H₆O₃ | Same empirical, different molecules | Why M_r is essential |
| Fertilizer grade | N-P-K % by weight | Urea 46-0-0, DAP 18-46-0, MOP 0-0-60 | Commercial spec language |
| Assay | Quantitative determination of main component | Titration, HPLC, spectroscopy | Quality control |
| Purity | % of desired substance in sample | Assay % = purity if single component | Commercial grade |
| CoA (Certificate of Analysis) | Official document with % composition, pass/fail | Legal requirement for trade | Buyer protection |
| Kjeldahl method | %N determination by digestion + distillation + titration | %N × 6.25 = % protein | Protein analysis standard |
| Gravimetric analysis | Precipitate → weigh → % | BaSO₄ for %SO₄, AgCl for %Cl | Classical accuracy |
| HPLC/GC/ICP | Instrumental % composition | Separation + detection + quantitation | Modern high-throughput |
| Isotope pattern | M+1, M+2 peaks in MS | Confirms molecular formula | HRMS verification |

- "Sum to 100 or start over".
- "12/44 for C, 2/18 for H, O by difference".
- "M_r = 2×VD".
- "1:2:1 smells like carbohydrate; verify with M_r".

- "Glucose proof: CH₂O ×6".
- "Urea 46.67% = 28/60; NH₄NO₃ 35% = 28/80".

## 10. Topic Mastery Check

### Important definitions
1. **Percentage composition** — mass % of each element in a compound; Σ% = 100.
2. **Forward calculation** — formula → % (known formula, compute %).
3. **Backward calculation** — % → formula (known %, find formula).
4. **Combustion analysis** — burn sample, weigh CO₂/H₂O → %C (×12/44), %H (×2/18), %O by difference.
5. **Vapour density** — mass of gas volume ÷ mass of same volume H₂; M_r = 2×VD.
6. **Empirical formula** — simplest whole-number atom ratio.
7. **Molecular formula** — actual atom numbers in one molecule.
8. **n = M_r/E_r** — multiplier from empirical to molecular.
9. **Assay** — quantitative determination of main component.
10. **Purity** — % of desired substance in sample.

### Key concepts to remember
- %E = (element mass per mole ÷ M_r) × 100; bars must sum to 100.
- Urea 46.67% N = 28/60 — the bag verified; NH₄NO₃ 35% N = 28/80.
- Combustion factors: C from CO₂ (×12/44), H from H₂O (×2/18), O by difference.
- n = M_r/E_r — needs measured M_r (VD×2, mass spec); never assumed.
- Empirical gives ratio, never identity (CH₂O family: glucose, formaldehyde, lactic acid).
- Ionic salts (NaCl) have empirical formulae only — no molecular formula.
- Quality audit: forward route verifies label; backward route identifies unknowns.

### Important classifications
- **Forward vs Backward:** Formula → % (audit) vs % → Formula (identification).
- **Organic vs Inorganic:** Combustion analysis for organics; gravimetric/titration for inorganics.
- **Volatile vs Non-volatile:** VD for volatiles; colligative/MS for non-volatiles.
- **Covalent vs Ionic:** Molecular + empirical vs empirical only.

### Important comparisons
| Basis | Forward (formula → %) | Backward (% → formula) |
|-------|----------------------|------------------------|
| Input | Known molecular formula | % composition from analysis |
| Output | % of each element | Empirical formula (+ molecular if M_r known) |
| Use | Quality audit, label check | Structure elucidation, unknown ID |
| Check | Sum to 100 | n = M_r/E_r must be integer |

| Method | M_r determination | Best for |
|--------|------------------|-----------
| Vapour density | M_r = 2×VD | Volatile liquids/gases |
| Mass spectrometry (HRMS) | Exact M_r from M⁺ | All volatile/ionizable |
| Colligative properties | ΔT_f, ΔT_b, π → M_r | Non-volatile solutes |
| Ideal gas law | PV = nRT → M_r = mRT/PV | Gases at known T/P |
| From formula | Σ A_r | When formula known |

### Common conceptual confusions
- Mass % ≠ mole % — convert with A_r before comparing.
- O by difference assumes only C, H, O present; N/S need separate estimation.
- Empirical gives ratio, never identity — CH₂O ×n family hides different molecules.
- Vapour density needs H₂ = 2 scale stated; M_r = 2×VD.
- Balance precision (±0.1 mg) decides analysis quality; ±0.001 g on 0.1 g sample = ±1%.
- Same empirical (CH₂O) ≠ same compound — glucose, formaldehyde, lactic acid all CH₂O.
- Ionic salts (NaCl) stop at empirical — no molecular formula for giant lattice.
- % yield >100% indicates impure product or incomplete drying, not excess product.

### Conceptual questions
1. Why must percentages sum to 100? What if they don't?
2. Can two different compounds have the same % composition? Explain.
3. Why is vapour density defined against H₂, not air?
4. How does combustion analysis work for compounds containing N or S?
5. What happens if n = M_r/E_r is not an integer?

### Application-based questions
1. 100 kg urea at ₹25/kg vs 100 kg NH₄NO₃ at ₹25/kg — which gives more N? By how much?
2. 4.4 g organic → 8.8 g CO₂ + 3.6 g H₂O. M_r = 88. Find molecular formula.
3. A limestone sample claims 45% Ca. Audit: CaCO₃ has 40% Ca. What does the claim imply?
4. Protein contains 16% N. A food has 3.2% N by Kjeldahl. What is its % protein?
5. Steel spec: 0.2% C max. A 5 tonne batch has 12 kg C. Pass or fail?

### Answers
1. %E = (mass of E per mole ÷ M_r) × 100; Σ%E = 100.
2. Urea CO(NH₂)₂, M_r = 60: %N = (2×14)/60 × 100 = 28/60 × 100 = 46.67%.
3. 40/12 = 3.33; 6.7/1 = 6.7; 53.3/16 = 3.33 → ÷3.33 → 1:2:1 → CH₂O.
4. VD = mass of gas volume / mass of same volume H₂; M_r = 2 × VD (H₂ = 2 scale).
5. %C = 8.8×12/44 × 100/4.4 = 54.55%; %H = 3.6×2/18 × 100/4.4 = 9.09%.
6. O by difference = 100 − Σ(other %); assumes only C,H,O,N,S,halogens — no unmeasured elements.
7. Urea: 46.67 kg N per 100 kg; NH₄NO₃: 35 kg N per 100 kg. Urea gives 11.67 kg more N per 100 kg at same price.
8. %C = 44×12/44 = 12% (if CO₂ is 44% of product mass — unclear question). Better: 4.4 g sample → 8.8 g CO₂ → %C = 54.55%; 3.6 g H₂O → %H = 9.09%; %O = 36.36% → C₂H₄O empirical; VD 44 → M_r 88 → n=2 → C₄H₈O₂.
9. Forward: formula → % (audit). Backward: % → formula (ID). Audit verifies 46% N on urea bag.
10. Kjeldahl: %N × 6.25 = % protein (avg protein 16% N → 1/0.16 = 6.25).
11. Urea gives 46.67 kg N; NH₄NO₃ gives 35 kg N per 100 kg. Urea wins by 11.67 kg N.
12. 4.4 g → 8.8 g CO₂ + 3.6 g H₂O → C₂H₄O empirical (E_r=44); VD=44 → M_r=88 → n=2 → C₄H₈O₂.
13. Claim 45% Ca > 40% theoretical max for CaCO₃ → implies impurity (e.g., CaO, Ca(OH)₂) or different mineral (not pure limestone).
14. %N = 3.2% → % protein = 3.2 × 6.25 = 20%.
15. 5 tonne = 5000 kg; 0.2% C = 10 kg max; 12 kg C = 0.24% → FAIL (exceeds spec).
16. Sum ≠ 100 means missing element or calculation error — re-check.
17. Yes — isomers (C₂H₆O: ethanol vs dimethyl ether) have same % composition. Also different compounds with same empirical formula (CH₂O family).
18. H₂ is the lightest gas, historically available pure, M_r = 2 exactly → simple integer scale (VD = M_r/2). Air is mixture, variable.
19. N/S measured separately (e.g., Dumas for N, Schöniger for S) and added to % sum; O by difference still used.
20. Non-integer n means: wrong M_r, wrong empirical, or impure sample — re-check all data.

### PYQ Solutions

**Q: Give the % composition formula and the sum rule. (2 marks)**
**Answer:** %E = (mass of E per mole ÷ M_r) × 100. The percentages of all elements in a compound must sum to 100.
**Keywords:** %E formula, mass per mole, M_r, sum to 100.

**Q: Prove urea is 46.67% nitrogen. (3 marks)**
**Answer:** Urea CO(NH₂)₂, M_r = 60. N mass per mole = 2×14 = 28. %N = 28/60 × 100 = 46.67%.
**Keywords:** urea formula, M_r 60, N mass 28, 28/60×100.

**Q: Derive CH₂O from 40% C, 6.7% H, 53.3% O data. (3 marks)**
**Answer:** Per 100 g: C 40/12 = 3.33 mol; H 6.7/1 = 6.7 mol; O 53.3/16 = 3.33 mol. Ratio ÷3.33 = 1:2:1 → CH₂O.
**Keywords:** per 100g, ÷A_r, ÷smallest, 1:2:1, CH₂O.

**Q: How is M_r obtained from vapour density? (2 marks)**
**Answer:** M_r = 2 × vapour density (VD), where VD = mass of a volume of gas ÷ mass of same volume of H₂ under same conditions. H₂ = 2 scale.
**Keywords:** M_r = 2×VD, H₂ = 2 scale.

**Q: From 8.8 g CO₂ + 3.6 g H₂O out of 4.4 g sample, find %C and %H. (3 marks)**
**Answer:** %C = 8.8 × 12/44 × 100/4.4 = 54.55%. %H = 3.6 × 2/18 × 100/4.4 = 9.09%.
**Keywords:** 12/44, 2/18, per sample mass.

**Q: Explain percentage composition with H₂SO₄ and urea computations. (5 marks)**
**Answer:** %E = mass E per mole ÷ M_r × 100; Σ% = 100. H₂SO₄ (M_r 98): %H=2/98×100=2.04%, %S=32/98×100=32.65%, %O=64/98×100=65.31%. Urea (M_r 60): %N=28/60×100=46.67%, %C=12/60×100=20%, %O=16/60×100=26.67%, %H=4/60×100=6.67%. The 46-0-0 fertilizer bag is urea's 46.67% N derived.
**Keywords:** formula, M_r, each %, sum 100, H₂SO₄ breakdown, urea 46.67%.

**Q: Derive empirical and molecular formulae from analysis data with combustion route. (5 marks)**
**Answer:** Burn 4.4 g sample → 8.8 g CO₂, 3.6 g H₂O. %C = 8.8×12/44×100/4.4 = 54.55%; %H = 3.6×2/18×100/4.4 = 9.09%; %O = 100−54.55−9.09 = 36.36%. Moles: C 4.55, H 9.09, O 2.27 → ratio 2:4:1 → C₂H₄O (E_r=44). If VD=44 → M_r=88 → n=2 → molecular C₄H₈O₂. If M_r=180 → n not integer — re-check data.
**Keywords:** combustion factors, %C/%H, O by diff, empirical, VD, n=M_r/E_r, molecular.

## 12. Summary and Self-check
% composition = element mass ÷ molar mass × 100, always summing to 100: H₂SO₄ (2.04/32.65/65.31), urea N 46.67% (the bag proved), NH₄NO₃ N 35%, CaCO₃ Ca 40%. Backward: % → grams → moles → ratio → empirical (CH₂O); with M_r (often 2×VD): n = M_r/E_r → molecular (C₆H₁₂O₆; M_r 90 → C₃H₆O₃). Combustion analysis gives %C (×12/44) and %H (×2/18), O by difference. Figures: composition bars, analysis-to-formula flow, analytical balance photo, carbon-12 mole reference.

**Self-check.** (1) Prove urea's 46% and compare with NH₄NO₃'s 35%. (2) 8.8 g CO₂ from 4.4 g sample → %C? (3) From C₂H₄O data plus M_r 88, give the molecular formula. (4) Why must O come "by difference"? (5) Audit: a "40% Ca" limestone claim — show the true value.

**Common confusions.** Mass % ≠ mole % (convert via A_r first) · empirical gives ratio, never identity (CH₂O ×n family) · vapour density needs the H₂ = 2 scale stated · balance precision (±0.1 mg) decides analysis quality.
